Kuvitus: opiskelija kävelee koulun tasai: Illustration: a student walks along a level school corridor with a heavy backpack on their back. The floor is horizontal, and a dashed arrow parallel to the floor shows the direction of travel. In the background there is a row of lockers and some windows.
Kaavakuva kahdesta tilanteesta. Vasemmal: Diagram of two situations. On the left a backpack is carried sideways: the supporting force F points up but the motion is sideways, so the force does no work, W = 0. On the right the backpack is lifted up: the force F and the motion are in the same direction, so the force does work W = F s.
Kaavakuva Joulen kokeesta. Putoava paino: Diagram of Joule's experiment. A falling weight pulls a string that passes over a pulley and turns a paddle wheel in a vessel of water. The force of the weight does work over the falling distance h, and the paddle wheel warms the water: work turns into heat.
Kaavakuva kahdesta (s,F)-kuvaajasta. Vas: Diagram of two (s,F) graphs. On the left the force is constant, and the work is the area of a rectangle F · s. On the right the force first increases steadily and then stays constant; the work is the area of a triangle A₁ plus the area of a rectangle A₂.
(s,F)-kuvaaja mittakaavassa: voima kasva: (s,F) graph to scale: the force increases linearly from zero to 40 newtons over 0–0.20 metres; the area of the triangle is the work.
Diagram of lifting work, not to scale. A box is lifted at a steady speed from the ground to a height h. The lifting force F points up and the weight G of the box points down, and the arrows are equally long, F = G. The lifting work is W = F h = G h.
